name: Glenn Grothman

statements.quote: Government use of Artificial Intelligence poses significant and potentially positive outcomes but also significant challenges – particularly surrounding ethical use and data security. I think it is the duty of Congress to examine both the positives and negatives of AI prior to authorizing what is likely to be billions of dollars for decades.
statements.venue: Opening remarks as Oversight National Security Subcommittee Ranking Member at AI hearing

statements.quote: We can see the dangers of run-away AI use in China. Using AI to support genocide in Xinjiang and suppress democracy in Hong Kong provides insight into how our adversaries view and use this technology – as a way to suppress dissent and to become a global economic and military power. It is vital that the U.S. counter these actions.
statements.venue: Opening remarks as Oversight National Security Subcommittee Ranking Member at AI hearing

statements.quote: These tools can be invaluable for augmenting worker safety, but there must be space for human oversight, and employers should be wary of delegating ultimate responsibility for worker safety to AI.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House Workforce Protections Subcommittee hearing on AI and workplace safety

statements.quote: How one looks at religion, it could affect how someone looks at politics, it could affect how someone looks at history. [...] And one of the things that scares me it people get a hold of this, you’ll push a politically correct view on all these topics.
statements.venue: Education and Workforce Committee hearing, as reported by Seehafer News

statements.quote: One of my concerns about A.I. is that it could lead to a decrease in human involvement in the workplace due to over-involvement in technology.
statements.venue: House Education and Workforce hearing on AI and higher education, as reported by Seehafer News

statements.quote: We recently passed a bill -- the Ratepayer Protection Act -- in Congress, which should make sure that new data centers were covering the charges for water, were covering the charges for electricity, and I think that will be a big step in the right direction,

We should pass laws preventing people from putting phony images of somebody on the internet. That being said, I'm not for as much regulation as some other people. Regulation benefits the big guy, right? I don't care what business you're in and we want new people in the field at all times.

- **Date estimated:** The Oversight subcommittee hearing statement has no date on the page. I put it at roughly 2021 because he was subcommittee ranking member and the witnesses discussed the National Security Commission on AI report.
- **Quote joined:** The October 2026 radio interview quote is joined from a timestamped transcript. I removed the line breaks and timestamps.
